customManagers.description: The version of the release-please schema, in the $schema of release-please-config.json and in the --schemafile argument of the check-jsonschema hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml. Both carry the same URL, so Renovate updates them in one pull request. The URL names a tag of googleapis/release-please, such as v17.6.0, and the releases of that repository are tagged the same way.

packageRules.description: Update ruff in pyproject.toml and the ruff-pre-commit hook in one pull request.
Update prek in pyproject.toml and the prek version passed to prek-action in one pull request.
Update zensical in pyproject.toml and the version that the check-docs-site hook installs in one pull request (a unit test checks that the two are the same).
Python stays on the version chosen in ADR-0012: changing it is a decision, not a routine update.
Runner images change on purpose, not as routine updates: the checks must support a new image first (actionlint validates runner labels).

Renovate's own image, run by .github/workflows/renovate.yml. Renovate reads Docker release dates only from Docker Hub, and this image is on GHCR, so the three-day wait cannot apply (expect a 'did not have a releaseTimestamp' warning on the Dependency Dashboard); Renovate releases almost daily, so its version is updated once a week; and the action input holds a version tag only, so the image is not pinned by digest.

The weekly refresh of uv.lock: Renovate leaves it to uv and cannot check the age of the releases in it, so the three-day wait does not apply (ADR-0012). Without this rule, Renovate (as of 44.132.5, October 2026) marks its pull request with a renovate/stability-days status that never clears (renovatebot/renovate#45236).
A new PostgreSQL major version needs its data upgraded (pg_upgrade, or a dump and a restore), so it is a decision with its own plan, not a routine update.

The images in compose.yaml and the base images in airflow/Dockerfile and caddy/Dockerfile are pinned by tag and digest. Official images are rebuilt often, so the updates that change only a digest come together, once a week.

Metabase publishes its hotfixes as four-part tags, such as v0.63.19.3, and its release notes name the floating v0.64.1.x tag. Renovate's docker versioning offers only tags with as many parts as the pinned one (as of 44.132.5, October 2026), so a pin on v0.64.1 would never get v0.64.1.1. This versioning sees the tags of three and of four parts, and leaves out the floating, beta and LTS tags, such as v0.64.x, v0.64.0.10-beta and v0.58-lts.
metabase-init and demo-init run on the Python version chosen in ADR-0012, so a new Python minor or major version of the python image is a decision, not a routine update.
The dbt lock file and the lock file of the container ai are regenerated by the pip-compile manager from their .in files; the pip_requirements manager must not edit their pins, which carry hashes.
A new minor or major version of dbt is a decision (ADR-0005): dbt Core and dbt-postgres move in step, and dbt 1.12 is the line that bridges to dbt v2.
The Airflow image of agoranomos is built from airflow/Dockerfile and has no registry to look up.
The Caddy image of agoranomos is built from caddy/Dockerfile and has no registry to look up.
The image of the container ai of agoranomos is built from ai/Dockerfile and has no registry to look up.
